# Rightmove.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/rightmove-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/rightmove-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects property listing data from Rightmove.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape RightMove Real Estate Property Data with Python](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-rightmove)
- **Code:** [`rightmove.py`](rightmove.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Property pages](results/properties.json) · [Search pages](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Rightmove property search for finding property listings
- Rightmove property pages for property listing data

## Functions

- `scrape_properties(urls)` → `List[PropertyResult]`: scrape Rightmove property listings for property data
- `scrape_search(location_name, location_id, scrape_all_properties, max_properties=1000)` → `dict`: scrape properties data from rightmove's search api

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import rightmove


async def main():
    properties = await rightmove.scrape_properties(
        urls=[
            "https://www.rightmove.co.uk/properties/149360984#/",
            "https://www.rightmove.co.uk/properties/136408088#/",
        ],
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`PropertyResult`**: `id`, `available`, `archived`, `phone`, `bedrooms`, `bathrooms`, `type`, `property_type`, `tags`, `description`, `title`, `subtitle`, `price`, `price_sqft`, `address`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `features`, `history`, `photos`, `floorplans`, `agency`, `industryAffiliations`, `nearest_airports`, `nearest_stations`, `sizings`, `brochures`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`rightmove.py`](rightmove.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"GB"`: country of the proxy

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/rightmove-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_search_scraping`, `test_properties_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
